New in version 16: role anchors. The app's minutes used to be too spread out: a high number finished lower and a low number finished higher, at every stage of a game. Each number is now pulled toward what a player in that role normally plays: tonight's starters, the bench, who is on the floor right now, and his own pace tonight. On this season's 121 games minutes land 21% closer at tip-off and 13 to 20% closer in the first quarter than the app as it was; points 3.5% closer at tip-off.

During a game a player still waiting to check in keeps the same kind of number as before tip-off: what he does if he gets in. Six minutes into a game used to be the app's weakest moment. It is now closer than tip-off, as it should be: minutes 20% closer, points 3.4% closer (121 games).

Late in a decided game the app reads who is actually on the floor. When the reserves are finishing the game, the regulars on the bench are done for the night and the reserves play it out. With three minutes left, minutes land 16% closer.

A lopsided score now costs a player more the more he usually plays, smoothly, instead of one rule for starters and one for everybody else. At halftime his first-half minutes count for more than before.

Before lineups post, deep-bench players get a number too (two of every three players who had no number and then played 10+ minutes were deep bench), and minutes nobody was going to play are no longer handed to teammates. Minutes land 15% closer before lineups, points 2.3% closer.
Tonight's starting five is inside every number from the moment lineups post. A reserve who starts gets his extra minutes, and a usual starter left out of the five is cut and flagged.
How crowded tonight's rotation is counts too: when several players are out, or everyone is back, minutes are not shared out evenly.

Points, rebounds and assists follow the minutes. Through the third quarter points land 1 to 3.5% closer and rebounds 0.6 to 3% closer on these 121 games; in the last six minutes the gain is less than 1%. A second, larger test on 592 of last season's games that the lessons never saw agrees at every stage (version 16 against version 15: minutes 3 to 13% closer, points up to 1.9%, rebounds up to 2.2%, assists up to 1.4%).

The projected final score ran 2 to 5 points low during games. A check learned from complete games now corrects half of that through the third quarter (592 unseen games: the total lands 2 to 5% closer from the first quarter to the end of the third).

What is left is mostly the bounce of the game. With the real minutes known in advance, points would still miss by about 4 at tip-off, and a second learning stage (boosted trees with the whole game state) could not get points, rebounds or assists closer than these numbers on unseen games. The app's numbers close in on the final line as the game goes: about 3.2 points at halftime, 2.2 after three quarters, 1.2 with six minutes left.
The lessons built into the app come from 3,709 games across four seasons: every final through Nov 9. Every plus edge shown is saved and graded on this phone: see EDGE RECORD above.
